label: A U-Net: down for context, up for detail, skips for both
context: Draw a U-Net schematically as feature-map stacks: on the left four encoder stages with square feature maps shrinking (e.g. 32, 16, 8, 4 cells per side, drawn as grids) and getting thicker (more channels, drawn as more stacked layers), a bottleneck at the bottom, four mirrored decoder stages on the right growing back. Phase 1: a 3×3 kernel square slides over the top-left map; then highlight the receptive field of one bottleneck cell, shown as a large region of the input image (caption 'every downsampling doubles how far a cell can see'). Phase 2: data flows down then up (animated pulses along arrows). Phase 3: pulses travel along the horizontal dashed skip connections from each encoder stage to its decoder stage (violet #6A47C2) with caption 'skips carry fine detail straight across'. Label 'encoder', 'decoder', 'bottleneck', 'skip'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: U-Net: down for context, up for detail, skips for both
spec.caption: Encoder stages halve the resolution and add channels, so each cell sees more of the image. The decoder grows the maps back. Skip connections copy fine detail from each encoder stage across to its decoder stage.
